days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday itself has some quiet gems. Partizanfilm on College Street runs a one night only screening of WTO/99 at 6:20, an archival documentary on the 40,000 strong 1999 Seattle protests against the World Trade Organization. Language lovers can drop into Spanish Chat Mondays at Three Needs from 7 to 8, all levels welcome. If you'd rather move than talk, pickup dodgeball runs 7 to 8:15 at the Miller Center for $5 a game, no team needed. Readers can join the Book Club For Curious Women [MEETUP] in Essex Junction at 6:30, where the whole month's homework is two chapters. And the Collage Collective gathers at Expressive Arts on Flynn Ave from 6:30 to 9, by donation, beginners welcome.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday is primary day in Vermont, so vote before you play. Polls run all day, and if an absentee ballot is still sitting on your counter the advice at this point is to hand it to your town clerk in person rather than mail it, more on that in the news below. The big musical event of the week also starts Tuesday, with Lake Street Dive opening a two night stand on the Shelburne Museum green at 7. Both nights are sold out, so this one is for ticket holders and wait list optimists, and kids 12 and under get in free without a ticket. Otherwise Tuesday leans social. Runners can lace up for the 5K at Queen City Brewery [MEETUP] at 5:30 with a beverage waiting at the finish, early birds can try the free morning networking hour at Hula at 8:30 with coffee on the house, and beginners with a sewing machine gathering dust can bring it to the free Sandbox sewing class on Pine Street from 4 to 5:30. Traditional Tuesday at Mesmer Kava pours all-you-like kava shells for a $20 flat fee from 4:30 to 8, Super Smash Tuesdays takes over RíRá from 5 with free play and a $10 smash burger, and French speakers get Pause-Café Mardi at Burlington Bay from 5 to 7.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday stacks up nicely. Lake Street Dive plays night two at Shelburne Museum, and downtown answers with Art Amplified , Burlington City Arts' free evening of live music with Troy Millette and the Fire Below and Collin Hagood at the BCA Center from 5. Comedy people have a full evening at Vermont Comedy Club, with the $5 Improv Night at 7 featuring Big Green Couch and an open jam after the show. Also on Wednesday, Local Motion is hosting the Ride for Shiloh at 5:30 . The community Critical Mass ride will meet at the memorial on the corner of Pine and Locust Streets to honor the 16-year-old BHS student whose tragic passing we’ve already covered. It’s a chance to support her family, remember her legacy, and stand together in support of safer streets for everyone. The Media Factory runs Audio Recording 101 from 6 to 8, a free hands-on tour of microphones and recording basics. Trivia lands at the Venetian Soda Lounge on Pine Street at 7, and artists can bring a sketchbook to Daydream Art Supply's Summer Sketchbook Club on Church Street from 5. Our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] runs at Pomeroy Park from 5:30, free and outdoors, come get a run in.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday is the fullest day on the calendar, so keep half an eye on the sky with storms in the forecast. Party On The Bricks throws its season finale on the Leahy Block from 5:30 to 8 with Ali T playing outside Ken's Pizza and Pub, free and open to all. South Burlington's SB Nite Out fills Veterans Memorial Park with food trucks and live music from 5:30 to 8, Williston gets a free John Fogerty tribute on the Maple Tree Place green at 6, and cyclists can head to the Bivo Summer Bash at Cochran's in Richmond from 5 to 8:30, with group rides followed by live music, sourdough pizza and Frost beers. Film lovers can celebrate Alfred Hitchcock's 127th birthday with Notorious at the VTIFF Screening Room at 7, and theater people get opening night of Falsettos ($14-35) at the Black Box Theater at 7, running through August 23. Music bingo plays at Sparky's in Essex Junction at 6:30, the Odd Fellows hall on North Ave hosts figure drawing with the Emanata Art Collective at 7, and night owls can two-step into the Thursday Night Social Club ($10, 21+) at Radio Bean, a 10:30 show from Americana six piece Andrea Maddox & The Hey Y'alls. We'll also be at Trivia at Four Quarters [MEETUP] in Winooski at 6, come early and help us hold a table.
